title: Rice husk derived graphene-like material: Activation with phosphoric acid in the absence of inert gas for hydrogen gas storage
material_description: GRHA 1:3 | rice-husk-derived graphene-like material (GRHA): rice husk carbonized at 350 °C for 2 h in a crucible (rice husk ash, RHA), impregnated with 3 M H3PO4 (GRHA:H3PO4 ratio 1:3) and activated at 700 °C for 2 h without inert gas (double-crucible method)
purification_method: raw rice husk washed and dried at 80 °C for 24 h before carbonization; after activation washed with warm distilled water, sonicated about 30 min, centrifuged at 4000 rpm until neutral pH, vacuum-filtered and dried 24 h at 80 °C
activation_method: H3PO4 chemical activation: about 5 g RHA mixed with 50 mL of 3 M H3PO4 at 80 °C for 2 h, dried 24 h at 100 °C, then calcined at 700 °C for 2 h in a muffle furnace in a double crucible compacted with ceramic wool and carbon powder (no inert gas)
functional_groups: FTIR: C=C (about 1627 cm-1), C=C and C=O (1700 and 1600 cm-1), vinyl =C-H (1000-1200 cm-1), C-H (about 800 cm-1); -OH band absent after activation
source_location: main p. 31093 (page main-10), Table 4, row GRHA 1:3, q_e,exp (mmol/g); main p. 31092 (page main-09), Table 3, row "GRHA" (This work); main p. 31091 (page main-08), Results "Hydrogen adsorption" text; equilibrium end point of kinetic curve in Fig. 10
notes: Table 4 prints q_e,exp = 973.9900 ± 0.0100% (mmol/g); text prints 'around 974 mmol/g (1.95 wt %)'. UNIT-CONSISTENCY FAILURE (protocol §3): W1 from 973.9900 mmol/g = 196.3 wt% and W2 = 66.3 wt%, neither matches the printed 1.95 wt%; the printed wt% equals about mmol/g x 0.002, so wt_pct_convention = unknown. Printed uncertainty "± 0.0100%" is relative and not in wt%, so uncertainty_wt_pct is empty. Kinetic fits of this run (Table 4): pseudo-first-order k1 = 0.1175, R2 = 0.9207; pseudo-second-order k2 = 0.2778, R2 = 0.9980; intraparticle diffusion k3 = 77.2635, R2 = 0.8577. Only uptake value of this sample at this temperature apart from the kinetic-model q_e,cal rows (same run, same pressure), so no isotherm_id. Temperature from Table 3 row "GRHA" (This work: 25.00 °C, 30.00 bar, 1.95 %), which reports this sample's measured uptake; highlights say "room temperature". Table 1: BET 315.07 m2/g, TPV 0.21, Vmicro 0.14, Vmicro/TPV 66.84 %, Vmeso 0.07 cm3/g, pore size 1.87 nm. Table 2 (XRD): d spacing 0.3985 ± 0.01 nm, crystallite size 0.4228 ± 0.01 nm. Fig. 7 Raman: ID/IG = 0.68, I2D/IG = 1.17. Material class follows the authors' identification as a graphene-like material ("rice husk derived graphene", GRHA); it is made by H3PO4 chemical activation of rice-husk char and XRD shows an amorphous structure, so activated_carbon is the alternative class. Pressure: the paper reports the test as at 30 bar (Table 3: 30.00 bar; Fig. 10 caption "at 30 bar"); methods say "The hydrogen is set at pressure 30 bar" in the loading column before expansion into the adsorption column, so the equilibrium pressure after expansion is not reported; gauge or absolute not stated. Uptake basis not named; volumetric (custom static volumetric rig) so basis_inferred = excess by instrumental default. Degassing before H2: "samples were placed overnight in an oven at 120 °C for drying purpose" (duration "overnight", no number; no vacuum stated). Sample mass printed as "GRHA was weighed at 1 g". No free-volume calibration or H2 purity stated. BET: N2 at 77 K (Quantachrome TouchWin), samples degassed at 150 °C overnight before BET; BET range and consistency criteria not stated. Pore volumes from N2 adsorption, method not stated; PSD by DFT; pore size (Table 1) taken as the DFT PSD value (text links 1.87 and 1.82 nm to Fig. 5 PSD). Mesopore volume = total pore volume - micropore volume (Table 1 footnote).
